look_here_first: Orange umbels alone do not prove butterfly milkweed: check typically alternate, hairy leaves and unusually clear/watery sap; tropical milkweed has opposite (sometimes irregularly grouped) smoother leaves, milky latex and usually red-orange corollas with contrasting yellow corona hoods.

key_traits.label: Sap type
key_traits.text: Clear to watery sap; notably lacks the typical milky latex of most Asclepias.

key_traits.label: Stem
key_traits.text: Stout, clustered from the crown, erect to spreading, conspicuously hairy/pilose.

key_traits.label: Leaf arrangement
key_traits.text: Alternate; leaves often crowded and can appear irregularly approximate.

key_traits.label: Leaf morphology
key_traits.text: Highly variable; narrow-lanceolate to broadly oblanceolate/oblong-lanceolate, usually 3–12 cm long, short-petiolate to nearly sessile, surfaces conspicuously hairy.

key_traits.label: Inflorescence
key_traits.text: Terminal to subterminal branching system bearing several- to many-flowered umbelliform cymes; overall cluster often rounded to flat-topped.

key_traits.label: Flower color
key_traits.text: Usually vivid orange; yellowish or reddish forms can occur.

key_traits.label: Gynostegium detail
key_traits.text: Orange to yellowish gynostegium; corona hoods contain horns. Corolla lobes are reflexed.

key_traits.label: Fruit
key_traits.text: Elongate follicle, gray-green to brownish, with short hairs; seeds comose.
